body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{np}}\), the map \(P\mapsto\Psi_\delta(P)\) is pathwise differentiable in the unrestricted observational model if and only if \(K_\delta(P)=0\). At every such regular law its canonical gradient is \(D_P\), its efficiency bound is \(V_P\), and \(D_P\) is uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on \(M\) and \(\delta\). If \(K_\delta(P)>0\), no regular asymptotically linear estimator with an ordinary root-\(n\) Gaussian limit exists at \(P\).
body.justification: The exact regularity frontier determines when efficient inference is mathematically available and when posterior Gaussian calibration is impossible.
body.gap: Luedtke and van der Laan characterize an outcome-rule kink; Zhou and Opacic define the capped propensity policy. Neither gives the propensity-kink criterion \(K_\delta(P)=0\) or this positivity-robust canonical gradient.
body.consumer: A practitioner can diagnose whether an atom in a discrete or heaped assignment score invalidates Wald or Gaussian posterior inference for the capped policy.
